mortgageSetup.title: Mortgage configuration
mortgageSetup.subtitle: Enter your loan's global parameters; the system will derive optimal split strategies from these.
mortgageSetup.targetTermDisabledTitle: Interest-only cannot infer term from payment
mortgageSetup.tipMaxTerm: Typical amortisation terms are 25 or 30 years.
mortgageSetup.tipPayment: Enter the per-period amount you want to deduct; the system will derive a sensible term at the current floating rate.
mortgageSetup.errorAmount: Total loan amount must be valid (≥ 1,000 NZD).
mortgageSetup.errorTerm: Repayment target must be between 1 year (12 months) and 30 years (360 months).
mortgageSetup.errorPayment: Per-period payment must be a valid number greater than 0.
mortgageSetup.hintTotalAmount: This is your total loan principal. For example, if you borrowed $600,000 for a property, enter 600000. The system generates split strategies based on this amount.
mortgageSetup.hintFrequency: Repayment frequency determines the interval between payments. Monthly is the most common in NZ. Fortnightly and Weekly options accelerate principal paydown with smaller per-period payments.
mortgageSetup.hintRepaymentType: Principal & Interest is the standard NZ choice — each payment covers both principal and interest. Interest Only defers principal repayment until later, useful when cash flow is tight.
mortgageSetup.hintTermMode: Choose how to define your repayment goal. "By expected payoff years" is most common — set a target term, and the system calculates your periodic payment. "By expected per-period payment" reverses this — set how much you can pay per period, and the system derives the required term.
mortgageSetup.hintStep2: This information directly affects the Strategy Lab simulation horizon (capped at your payoff term) and the default affordable payment budget. You can fine-tune these later in the lab.
about.title: About RatePath
about.subtitle: Learn about RatePath's local-first design, market configuration, and terms of use.

about.features.multiScenario: Multi-scenario interest simulation: builds low / base / high future OCR paths from four sliders (12-month change, medium-term direction, change speed, uncertainty) and aggregates expected metrics by user-set probability weights.
about.features.monteCarlo: Monte Carlo long-term paths: random samples beyond month 36 generate a distribution of possibilities; each run is a probabilistic outcome, not a prediction of future facts.
about.features.splitEnumerate: Split enumeration and ranking: exhaustively lists candidate splits under your max-splits, floating-cap, fixed-floor, and amount-floor constraints, then sorts by Pareto multi-objective (cost, worst-case interest, worst-case payment, refix concentration, budget breaches, principal paydown speed, floating share).
about.features.realtimeWeights: Real-time preference weighting: 8 preference-weight sliders steer the 'Preference-matched' card live without re-running the simulation.
about.features.localCompute: Local computation and storage: all amortisation, scoring, and ranking runs in your device's background thread (Web Worker); results are written only to your IndexedDB / localStorage.

about.privacyIntro: RatePath follows a strict 'local-first' privacy principle:

about.privacyBullets.noUpload: Zero data upload: every loan amount, tranche balance, interest rate, and extra-repayment plan you enter is stored only in your current browser's local IndexedDB and is never sent to any cloud server.
about.privacyBullets.noBackend: No backend design: the system has no backend database for collecting user information and does not require registration or login.
about.privacyBullets.sandbox: Sandbox: all mortgage amortisation, split probability scoring, and Pareto frontier filtering run in your device's background thread (Web Worker).

about.disclaimerIntro: Before using RatePath, please understand: this is a locally-run mathematical simulation tool and does not provide any form of financial advice or guarantee.

about.disclaimerBullets.noWarranty: Simulation only; no warranty: every curve, number, and ranked recommendation is a parameterised mathematical calculation or Monte Carlo random sample, and does not represent a forecast, quote, or endorsement from the RBNZ, any commercial bank, or any authoritative body.
about.disclaimerBullets.drift: Results may deviate materially from reality: expected interest, payment volatility, and ending balance depend on the assumptions, probability weights, and model parameters you supply; macro policy, inflation, and bank liquidity are not modelled.
about.disclaimerBullets.notAdvice: Not financial advice: the recommendations (preference-matched, lowest-cost, most-stable) are purely mathematical orderings and do not constitute professional financial, lending, tax, or legal advice.
about.disclaimerBullets.userRisk: User bears the decision risk: before signing any loan contract, fixing a rate, or making extra repayments, rely on the bank's official offer and consult a licensed professional.
about.disclaimerBullets.noLiability: No liability: to the maximum extent permitted by law, we disclaim all liability for any direct or indirect loss arising from the use of, inability to use, or reliance on this app's outputs.

opt.pro.costLow: Expected interest cost is very low; best in class for interest control.
opt.con.costHigh: Expected total interest cost is on the high side.
opt.pro.div.costPremium: Diversification preset: total cost is slightly above the optimum, in exchange for lower refix concentration and higher flexibility.
opt.pro.stabilitySmooth: Payment volatility is low; cash flow is predictable and well-supported.
opt.con.peakRisk: High-rate scenarios expose larger payment peaks (monthly / fortnightly / weekly).
opt.pro.paymentPayoffClean: Loan is paid off within a reasonable horizon, with no long-tail balance risk.
opt.con.paymentPayoffUnfinished: Loan is not fully paid off within the simulation horizon; balance tail risk exists.
opt.pro.term.principalFast: Principal paydown is fast; remaining balance drops quickly.
opt.con.term.principalSlow: Principal paydown is slow; ending balance is high.
opt.con.term.peakRisk: High-rate scenarios expose larger payment peaks (monthly / fortnightly / weekly).
opt.con.term.breachHigh: Budget overage count is high under stress scenarios; cash flow is squeezed.
opt.con.term.budgetHigh: Simulated budget overage count is on the high side; payment is squeezed under stress.
opt.pro.refix.spread: Refix dates are spread across different months; avoids a concentrated repricing shock.
opt.con.refix.concurrent: Multiple tranches mature together; refix exposure is concentrated.
opt.pro.div.refixSpread: Diversification preset: refix risk is spread across different months, so a single shock is more controllable.
opt.con.div.multiTranche: Diversification preset: managing multiple fixed-maturity dates is slightly more complex; track each sub-loan's refix timing.
opt.pro.div.flexPreserve: Diversification preset: ample floating / Offset headroom is preserved for opportunistic repayments or hedging.
opt.con.div.costPremium: Diversification preset: total cost is slightly above the optimum, in exchange for lower refix concentration and higher flexibility.
opt.pro.flex.high: High floating share keeps funds flexible; large extra repayments and offset top-ups are easy to apply.
opt.con.flex.locked: High fixed share locks in the loan; on-demand offset and large extra repayments are constrained.
opt.pro.endingBalanceLow: Under extreme scenarios, the ending principal balance is small; debt reduction is steady.
opt.con.endingBalanceHigh: Under extreme scenarios, the ending principal balance is high; paydown is uncertain.
opt.pro.volatilityLow: Payment stream has small month-to-month variance; cash flow is predictable.
opt.con.volatilityHigh: Payment stream is volatile; near-refix jumps are large — keep a buffer.
opt.pro.budgetLow: Simulated budget overage count is low; payment pressure stays controllable.
opt.pro.balanced: All financial and risk metrics are roughly balanced.
opt.con.noTailDefense: Lacks a deep defensive buffer against an extreme high-rate path.

legal.disclaimer.s1.title: 1. Tool nature
legal.disclaimer.s1.p1: RatePath provides mathematical calculation, scenario modelling, and result comparison. Its outputs are based on:
legal.disclaimer.s1.l2: Interest-rate scenarios you choose or adjust;
legal.disclaimer.s1.l5: Probability, term, repayment, and product-rule assumptions.
legal.disclaimer.s1.p2: Outputs describe simulated results that may occur if the specific assumptions hold; they are not statements about future facts.
legal.disclaimer.s1a.title: 1A. Probabilistic nature of Monte Carlo simulation
legal.disclaimer.s1a.p1: RatePath uses Monte Carlo random sampling for the long-term path beyond month 36:
legal.disclaimer.s1a.l1: Each run draws a set of sample paths from the user-defined uncertainty band; outputs may differ between runs;
legal.disclaimer.s1a.l2: Monte Carlo outputs only describe the probability distribution (e.g. quantiles, confidence intervals), not any 'most likely' or 'should happen' future path;
legal.disclaimer.s1a.l3: Sample size, random seed, and the sampling distribution are determined by the RatePath model internals; not a statistical model of any real economic process.
legal.disclaimer.s1b.title: 1B. Scenario probability weights are user-controlled
legal.disclaimer.s1b.p1: The low / base / high OCR paths and their probability weights (default 15% / 70% / 15%) are set or adjusted by you — not derived from any market-data source, central bank, or third party:
legal.disclaimer.s1b.l1: RatePath does not fetch, store, or validate the weight values you enter;
legal.disclaimer.s1b.l2: Changing the weights does not mean market expectations have changed; it only changes the mix you view when you look at aggregate expected metrics;
legal.disclaimer.s1b.l3: The aggregated 'expected' metrics are mathematical weighted results, not statistical estimates of real-world probabilities.
legal.disclaimer.s2.title: 2. No guarantee of future rates or results
legal.disclaimer.s2.p1: The Official Cash Rate (OCR), swap rate, bank funding cost, bank margin, and mortgage offers may change at any time. Historical data, official forecasts, market expectations, and statistical relationships do not guarantee future performance.
legal.disclaimer.s2.p2: All amounts, terms, savings amounts, payoff dates, risk scores, and probabilities are model estimates with no warranty of accuracy or reasonableness. Actual results may differ materially from model results, including but not limited to: rate increases, declined loans, contract terms that do not match the model assumptions, and changes in bank policy.
legal.disclaimer.s2a.title: 2A. Model limitations
legal.disclaimer.s2a.p1: RatePath's model has the following known limitations; any decision that ignores these limitations and relies on the output is at the user's own risk:
legal.disclaimer.s2a.l1: OCR transmission coefficients (Betas) are statistical estimates based on historical observations and do not guarantee that future bank quotes will track OCR with the same magnitude;
legal.disclaimer.s2a.l2: Paths beyond month 36 use Monte Carlo sampling + a smooth trend by default, and do not represent any specific macroeconomic scenario;
legal.disclaimer.s2a.l3: Fixed product rates are re-priced at refix using the current-month OCR level, and do not model bank-internal liquidity premia, relationship pricing, or promotional rates;
legal.disclaimer.s2a.l4: Repayment-frequency matching in the amortiser follows the 'matches mortgage frequency' rule and does not support per-extra-repayment independent frequencies;
legal.disclaimer.s2a.l5: Target-payment mode (payment-mode) only triggers overpayment when explicitly enabled, and does not equal an immediate offset-account write-off;
legal.disclaimer.s2a.l6: The model does not model tax, insurance, rate caps / collars, FX, cross-currency loans, or court freezes.

legal.privacy.title: RatePath Privacy Notice
legal.privacy.s1.title: 1. Overview
legal.privacy.s1.p1: RatePath is a purely locally-run mortgage-strategy simulation tool. All calculations happen in your browser or app; everything you enter is stored only on your own device.
legal.privacy.s1.p2: RatePath has no backend server, does not collect your mortgage data, does not collect your personal information, and will not actively upload anything you enter to any cloud.
legal.privacy.s2.title: 2. What we store on your device
legal.privacy.s2.p1: The following data lives only on your current browser's or app's local storage by default:
legal.privacy.s2.l1: Mortgage configuration (IndexedDB): total loan amount, tranche balances, interest rates, remaining term, repayment type (P&I / interest-only), repayment frequency, extra-repayment plan;
legal.privacy.s2.l2: Scenarios and strategies (IndexedDB): custom interest-rate scenarios you save in the Strategy Lab, split constraints, recommendation preference weights;
legal.privacy.s2.l3: Simulation results (IndexedDB): simulation runs and ranked outputs you actively save;
legal.privacy.s2.l4: Market rates (IndexedDB + localStorage): your custom values for the OCR and each mortgage product rate;
legal.privacy.s2.p2: This data is fully under your control. You can delete it at any time by clearing your browser's site data, clearing local storage, or uninstalling the app. Once deleted, we have no way to recover it.
legal.privacy.s3.title: 3. What we do not collect
legal.privacy.s3.p1: RatePath is a static front-end app. It does not:
legal.privacy.s3.l1: Ask for your account, email, phone number, or any identity credentials;
legal.privacy.s3.l2: Upload your mortgage inputs, simulation results, or preference data to any first- or third-party server;
legal.privacy.s3.l3: Integrate any analytics, advertising, or behaviour-tracking scripts;
legal.privacy.s3.l4: Integrate crash-reporting, performance monitoring, A/B testing, or similar telemetry services;
legal.privacy.s3.l5: Use any tracking cookies or similar identifiers;
legal.privacy.s3.l6: Provide accounts, subscriptions, paid features, in-app purchases, or login;
legal.privacy.s3.l7: Share, sync, or exchange any data between users.
legal.privacy.s3.p2: Because RatePath itself makes no business requests to any backend, it does not actively log or store your IP address, device identifier, browser fingerprint, or access log. Note: the service that hosts the RatePath site (e.g. a cloud platform or ISP) may, under its own policies, record basic network request logs (e.g. source IP, request time); that falls under the host's practices, not RatePath's.
legal.privacy.s4.title: 4. Local computation
legal.privacy.s4.p1: All mortgage amortisation, interest-scenario generation, split enumeration, simulation matrix execution, and Pareto ranking run only in your device's memory and background thread (Web Worker), with no dependency on any remote service.
legal.privacy.s5.title: 5. Your control
legal.privacy.s5.p1: Because RatePath does not hold any of your data:
legal.privacy.s5.l1: To view or modify your local data, use the browser developer tools directly; to export a backup, use the browser's IndexedDB / localStorage export capability (RatePath itself does not provide an export feature);
legal.privacy.s5.l2: To delete local data, use the browser's 'Clear site data' feature, or stop using RatePath;
legal.privacy.s5.l3: If you believe RatePath holds your personal information (it does not), you may still lodge a complaint with the New Zealand Office of the Privacy Commissioner under the Privacy Act 2020.
legal.privacy.s6.title: 6. Local data security
legal.privacy.s6.p1: The security of local data depends on your device's overall security posture, including but not limited to device lock, OS updates, browser security settings, backup habits, and whether you use the app on a shared device.
legal.privacy.s6.p2: RatePath loads its static assets over HTTPS, but does not transmit any user data externally. No online service can guarantee absolute security; please avoid saving sensitive financial information on untrusted devices or public networks.
legal.privacy.s7.title: 7. Co-borrowers / third-party data
legal.privacy.s7.p1: RatePath is aimed at adults able to make lending decisions independently. Do not enter the personal information of co-borrowers, guarantors, minors, or other third parties without authorisation.
legal.privacy.s7.p2: If you enter information on behalf of another person, you confirm that you have the appropriate authorisation and have explained the relevant processing to that person.
legal.privacy.s8.title: 8. Changes
legal.privacy.s8.p1: We may update this notice to reflect changes in features, dependencies, or law. Material changes will be reflected in the version number and effective date noted at the top of this page. We recommend reviewing this page periodically. Continued use of RatePath after a version update indicates your acceptance of the then-current version.

strategyLab.step7.title: OCR forecast scenario curves
strategyLab.step7.howToReadBody1: This chart updates live with the left-side input — no need to run a simulation first. The OCR forecast is built from a Monte Carlo pool: the system draws your configured sample count (default 200 × 3 families = 600 paths) for the low / base / high families. Months 0–12 follow a deterministic power curve so all samples coincide; months 13–36 layer Box–Muller normal shocks with 18% mean reversion toward the deterministic anchor; months 37+ enter cycle-based oscillations governed by your long-term cycle length, reversal bias, and uncertainty.
strategyLab.step7.howToReadBody2: The three solid lines are statistical percentiles of those 600 samples at every month — P10 in green (lower band edge: only 10% of samples fall at or below), P50 in the primary indigo (the median, most-probable case), P90 in rose (upper band edge: 90% of samples fall at or below). The translucent fill between P10 and P90 is the 90% confidence band; it widens with horizon, reflecting the intuition that further-out predictions are less certain. The white dashed line is the probability-weighted expected path over P10/P50/P90 using your scenario weights, and drives the default aggregate recommendation. Adjust the Monte Carlo sample count slider in Group 3 to trade chart fidelity for slider responsiveness; the simulation matrix underneath always runs against exactly 4 scenarios (P10, P50, P90, expected), so it stays flat regardless of this value.
strategyLab.step7.term.ocr.label: OCR
strategyLab.step7.term.ocr.body: New Zealand's Official Cash Rate. Not a mortgage rate itself, but it drives floating rates and fixed-rate refix pricing.
strategyLab.step7.term.weighted.label: Probability-weighted expected path
strategyLab.step7.term.weighted.body: White dashed line. Month-by-month weighted average of the low / base / high paths using your weights; drives expected interest and expected balance.
strategyLab.step7.term.optimistic.label: Long-term optimistic path
strategyLab.step7.term.optimistic.body: Long-term representative path with low rates. Conceptually close to the 10th-percentile (P10) sample — the optimistic side.
strategyLab.step7.term.median.label: Long-term median path
strategyLab.step7.term.median.body: Long-term representative path with median rates. Conceptually close to the 50th-percentile (P50) sample — the median.
strategyLab.step7.term.stress.label: Long-term stress path
strategyLab.step7.term.stress.body: Long-term representative path with high rates. Conceptually close to the 90th-percentile (P90) sample — the stress side.
strategyLab.step7.term.monteCarlo.label: Monte Carlo
strategyLab.step7.term.monteCarlo.body: Rather than guessing a single future line, we generate many possible paths and extract representative samples plus statistics.
strategyLab.step7.example1: If the weights are low 50% / base 30% / high 20%, the white dashed line sits closer to the low-rate path because it represents the weighted average of the three medium-term scenarios, not any one of them.
strategyLab.step7.example2: If months 13-36 trend up overall and the long-term reversal probability is 70%, the first long-term sample after month 37 is more likely to dip first, but it won't be a rigid line — up/down noise is preserved.
strategyLab.step7.example3: Long-term optimistic / median / stress are not fixed percentage moves and not user-set probability weights; they are three representative paths picked from the long-term samples.
strategyLab.step7.example4: Each family line is one continuous line: smooth 0–36 is your medium-term read, the noisier 37+ portion is the long-term MC continuation. The faded P10 / P50 / P90 series are independent representative samples — their monthly path may differ from the family line, that is expected.
strategyLab.step7.example5: The detail table below is in 1:1 correspondence with the chart. Switch to the "Long-term median path" and the table's interest, max payment, and ending principal all change to that path's results.
strategyLab.step8.title: Strategy simulation
strategyLab.step8.body: The system will generate valid strategies under at most {maxSplits} splits and at most {maxFloatingPercentage}% floating / Offset share, and run a {months}-month cash-flow analysis under three future rate scenarios.
strategyLab.step9.title: Pareto recommendations — optimal strategy per axis
strategyLab.step9.intro: The system independently picks the mathematical optimum for each Pareto axis (weights-independent), so you can see the trade-offs across dimensions. The 2 baseline cards are: Lowest expected cost / Most stable payment.
strategyLab.step9.preferenceCardStrong: The "Composite preference" card at the bottom
strategyLab.step9.preferenceCardTail: responds live to the {n} weight sliders above. All weights sum to 100%, each capped at 25% (forcing at least 4 dimensions to be considered). When you raise one, the others rescale proportionally.
strategyLab.step9.recommendMulti: Recommendation cards by default only pick from real split strategies with ≥ 2 tranches; 100% single-product strategies stay in the table below as a benchmark.
strategyLab.step9.recommendSingle: Current setting is 1 split, so only single-term-locked strategies are compared.
strategyLab.step9.clickCta: Click any card to open the detail modal and view the full timeline and comparison analysis.
strategyLab.shortTermChange.label: 12-month interest-rate change
strategyLab.shortTermChange.explanation: Cumulative change to the RBNZ OCR official discount rate projected over the next 12 months. Months 1-12 are smoothly interpolated (e.g. reflecting the 6-month transition).
strategyLab.shortTermChange.example1: Example: if the current OCR is 2.25%, setting this to -2.00% means OCR falls to 0.25% by month 12, and to ~1.25% by month 6.
strategyLab.shortTermChange.example2: Note: 1-year and 2-year fixed-term products do NOT follow this slider month-by-month while locked; at refix they re-price based on that month's OCR change vs the current OCR.
strategyLab.mediumTermDirection.label: Medium-term rate trajectory
strategyLab.mediumTermDirection.explanat: Between month 13 and month {n}, the policy rate follows the medium-term trend set by this slider. 1.0 unit of change corresponds to a 0.50%/year rate change.
strategyLab.mediumTermDirection.example: Example: -1.0 means the rate drops by 0.50% per year from month 13 to month 36; 0.0 means it stays flat from month 13 onward.
strategyLab.changeSpeed.label: Policy adjustment speed
strategyLab.changeSpeed.explanation: Time-distribution curve of the rate change over the next 12 months (i.e. how quickly the change actually happens).
strategyLab.changeSpeed.example: Example: 100% means the change is concentrated at month 1; 50% means linear over 12 months; 0% means slow at first and accelerating into month 12.
strategyLab.uncertainty.label: Uncertainty band
strategyLab.uncertainty.explanation: Width of the symmetric fan that, after month 3, widens to 25% at month 6 and 100% at month ≥12. Larger values spread the low / base / high scenarios further apart.
strategyLab.uncertainty.example: Example: at 2%, the high-rate path sits about 2% above base by month 12; at 0%, low and high collapse onto base.
strategyLab.scenarioProb.label: Scenario probability weights (%)
strategyLab.scenarioProb.warnTotal: The three weights must sum to 100%.
strategyLab.longTermCycle.label: Long-term cycle length (years)
strategyLab.longTermCycle.explanation: Average cycle length used by the Monte Carlo samples for the long-term tail (after month 36). A 2-year cycle oscillates faster than a 4-year cycle.
strategyLab.longTermCycle.example: Example: 4 years = slower wave around the central trend, more persistent regiemes.
strategyLab.longTermReversal.label: Long-term reversal probability
strategyLab.longTermReversal.explanation: Probability that the long-term sample reverses direction on a typical month. 0% = pure trend, 100% = near-random walk.
strategyLab.longTermReversal.example: Example: 70% means the long-term path frequently switches between rising and falling segments, instead of marching steadily in one direction.
strategyLab.simDuration.label: Simulation horizon (years)
strategyLab.simDuration.cappedByMortgage: Capped at the next whole year above your expected payoff ({n} yr).
strategyLab.simDuration.explanation: Months simulated for each (strategy, scenario) pair. Hard-capped at 10 years; further capped at the next whole year above your expected payoff.
strategyLab.monteCarloSampleCount.label: Monte Carlo sample count
strategyLab.monteCarloSampleCount.explan: Number of long-term Monte Carlo paths drawn per forecast. Used only to derive the P10 / P50 / P90 confidence band on the OCR chart — the simulation matrix stays at 4 scenarios (P10, P50, P90, expected) regardless of this value.
strategyLab.monteCarloSampleCount.exampl: More samples produce a smoother percentile band but slow slider feedback. Default 200 is a balanced speed / smoothness point.
strategyLab.maxSplits.label: Maximum number of splits
strategyLab.maxSplits.explanation: Upper bound on the number of tranches the strategy generator can produce (1 = single product, 3 = up to three). Larger values enrich the Pareto set but raise the simulation count.
strategyLab.maxSplits.example: Example: 3 lets the generator produce combinations like 30/40/30 across three different products; 1 only allows single-product strategies.
strategyLab.percentageStep.label: Combination grid step
strategyLab.percentageStep.explanation: Granularity of the percentage grid used to enumerate splits. 5% = fine, 10% = default, 15% = coarse. Finer grids produce more candidates.
strategyLab.percentageStep.example: Example: 15% only emits combinations like 50/35/15 instead of 53/32/15; cuts the candidate count by ~3x at 3 splits.
strategyLab.maxFloatingPct.label: Maximum floating / Offset share
strategyLab.maxFloatingPct.explanation: Cap on the floating-rate (Floating / Offset / Revolving Credit) share. The system also guarantees a minimum fixed share of {minFixed}% (= 1 - floating share), and the strategy generator derives that constraint internally.
strategyLab.maxFloatingPct.example: Example: at 10%, the loan can have at most 10% floating; the other 90% must be locked to a fixed term.
strategyLab.maxPayment.label: Per-period payment budget cap
strategyLab.maxPayment.explanation: Maximum per-period payment you can afford. Used to count 'budget overage' instances under high-rate scenarios and feeds the composite score.
strategyLab.maxPayment.example: Example: 5,000 with fortnightly frequency; if a high-rate fortnightly payment hits 5,200 the system records one overage.
strategyLab.diversification.presetTitle: Diversification preset — richer candidate set with refix-spread priority
strategyLab.diversification.explanation: When enabled, the strategy generator produces a richer candidate set (more splits, finer step, higher floating cap) and the optimiser weights refix-spread higher. The pros/cons on the recommendation cards switch to diversification-flavoured copy.
strategyLab.preferenceIntro: The {n} weights below always sum to 100%. When you raise one, the others rescale proportionally. Affects only the 'Preference-matched' card; the rate-simulation parameters and other cards are unchanged.
strategyLab.weightKeys.costExplain: Higher values favour strategies with the lowest total interest.
strategyLab.weightKeys.refixExplain: Higher values favour strategies that spread tranche maturity across different months.
strategyLab.weightKeys.flexExplain: Higher values try to use the allowed floating / Offset headroom to the maximum.
strategyLab.weightKeys.balanceExplain: Rewards spreads that avoid 90-10 extremes. Higher weight → balanced splits outrank 90-10 fixed-heavy splits on cost.
strategyLab.weightKeys.worstCaseDefenseE: Composite worst-case defense (worst interest + worst breaches + worst payment). Absorbs the former `resilience`, `budget`, `smoothness`, and `principal` axes (now removed for simplicity — they were strict subsets or highly correlated with this composite). Raising this slider steers the Preference-matched card toward strategies that hold up best under extreme scenarios.

strategyLab.warnHighSim.tip1: Lower 'Maximum splits': currently {cur} → recommend ≤ 3 (saves ~{pct}% of candidates)
strategyLab.warnHighSim.tip2: Increase 'Combination grid step': currently {cur}% → recommend 15% (saves ~{pct}% of candidates)
strategyLab.warnHighSim.tip3: Shorten 'Simulation horizon': currently {cur} yr → recommend ≤ 5 yr
strategyLab.warnHighSim.tip4: Tighten 'Maximum floating / Offset share': currently {cur}% → recommend ≤ 30% (saves ~{pct}% of floating branches)
strategyLab.warnHighSim.tipFinal: Constraints are already tight; if you need to keep them, click 'Start simulation' and accept the ~{n}+ sec compute time.

strategyLab.warnRunning.body: Above the {threshold} warning threshold. Either wait for the current run to finish, or cancel and tighten splits, increase step, or shorten horizon.

strategyLab.methodology.title: Methodology
strategyLab.methodology.summary: The chart on the right combines three short/medium OCR scenarios (low / base / high) and (when the horizon > 3 years) a Monte Carlo tail with representative optimistic / median / stress samples. White dashed line = probability-weighted expected path; coloured solid lines = scenario family paths; pale lines = individual Monte Carlo samples.
strategyLab.methodology.mc.title: Monte Carlo
strategyLab.methodology.mc.body: Rather than guessing a single future line, we generate many possible paths and extract representative samples plus statistics.
strategyLab.methodology.example1: If the weights are low 50% / base 30% / high 20%, the white dashed line sits closer to the low-rate path because it represents the weighted average of the three medium-term scenarios, not any one of them.
strategyLab.methodology.example2: If months 13-36 trend upward overall, and the long-term reversal probability is 70%, the first long-term sample after month 37 is more likely to dip first, but it won't be a rigid line — up/down noise is preserved.
strategyLab.methodology.example3: Long-term optimistic / median / stress are not fixed percentage moves and not user-set probability weights; they are three representative paths picked from the long-term samples.
strategyLab.methodology.example4: If the month-36 low-rate scenario sits at a low level but the long-term optimistic path starts from a higher position, you'll see a 'gap'. That's because the optimistic path is a representative sample, not a direct extension of the low-rate green line.

strategyLab.proAdvice.title: 📖 Professional split-strategy advice and rationale
strategyLab.proAdvice.q1.l1.title: Rate-shock protection
strategyLab.proAdvice.q1.l1.body: If the entire loan is locked in a single fixed term, when it matures during a high-rate cycle, the whole balance is exposed to higher interest at once. Splitting across terms makes different tranches mature in different years, spreading and diluting the rate-shock impact.
strategyLab.proAdvice.q1.l2.title: Smooth cash flow and capital flexibility
strategyLab.proAdvice.q1.l2.body: Short fixed terms (6 months, 1 year) let you benefit from any rate-cutting cycle. Long fixed terms (3 years, 5 years) lock down a ceiling on future payments and offer high predictability. The floating-rate portion, meanwhile, makes it easy to make large extra repayments or use an Offset account to offset interest — keeping capital flexible.
strategyLab.proAdvice.q2: How to pick the best split for you?
strategyLab.proAdvice.q2.l1.title: Filter the Pareto front first
strategyLab.proAdvice.q2.l1.body: The 'Optimal' badge in the exhaustive list below marks mathematically Pareto-optimal combinations. At the same interest cost, these have the lowest payment volatility; at the same volatility, they have the lowest total interest. Dominated options usually have a better alternative at every metric — they shouldn't be preferred.
strategyLab.proAdvice.q2.l2.title: Build a tranche ladder
strategyLab.proAdvice.q2.l2.body: In the NZ market, the typical recommendation is a 'laddered lock' (e.g. 30% locked 1 year, 50% locked 2 years, 20% floating / Offset). This both takes advantage of medium-term rate discounts and lets you re-fix or repay principal every 12 months based on how the market moves.

strategyLab.report.intro: Composite score: the system normalises and weights each strategy by your preference weights; lower score = better overall.Pareto-optimal: at the same interest cost the lowest-volatility, or at the same volatility the lowest-interest strategy, marked Optimal.Dominated: there exists another strategy no worse on every axis and strictly better on at least one.

strategyLab.probability.explanation: These three are not rate moves, and they do not directly reshape the low / base / high OCR curves. They are the probability weights the model uses when aggregating results: the system simulates each OCR path independently, then combines them by these proportions to produce metrics like expected interest, expected max payment, and ending principal, and they steer the default probability-weighted recommendation.
strategyLab.probability.exampleWorked: Worked example: a split with $140,000 / $160,000 / $190,000 of total interest under low / base / high scenarios, with the default 15% / 70% / 15% weights, gives expected interest = 140,000 × 15% + 160,000 × 70% + 190,000 × 15% = $161,500.
strategyLab.probability.exampleAdjustmen: Adjustment example: if you are more worried about high rates, raise the high-rate weight and the recommendation will lean toward payment pressure and ending principal under high rates; if you expect cuts, raise the low-rate weight and the recommendation will favor lower-cost splits under low-rate environments.
strategyLab.probability.exampleNote: Note: the three weights auto-balance to 100%. The default is low 15% / base 70% / high 15%.
strategyLab.longTerm.cycleExplain: Determines the dominant wave period of the long-term Monte Carlo path beyond month 36. With a 2-year cycle: if months 13-36 trend up, months 37-60 are more likely to turn down, then months 61-84 likely turn up again.
strategyLab.longTerm.reversalExplain: If the medium-term trend over months 13-36 is upward, the first long-term cycle preferentially turns down with this probability; if downward, it preferentially turns up with the same probability. Otherwise the model keeps same-direction volatility possible.
strategyLab.horizon.horizonExplain: Sets the future horizon that the strategy simulation covers. Rate changes and repayment calculations are calibrated to this period.
strategyLab.horizon.horizonCappedExample: 👉 Your mortgage-setup "expected payoff years" is about {target} yr ({months} mo). The system has auto-clamped the slider's upper bound to {max} yr (covering through the end of the target year). To adjust, return to the Mortgage Setup page.
strategyLab.horizon.horizonExample: Example: drag to 3 yr and the analysis covers only the next 36 months, computing ending principal at month 36.
strategyLab.constraints.presetDefaultTip: Conservative: 3 splits, 10% step, 10% floating cap, ~36 candidates
strategyLab.constraints.presetDiversific: Surfaces more 60/20/20 cross-term splits, ~500 candidates, auto-expands the report
strategyLab.constraints.presetMaxTip: Allows 50% floating and 5 splits, ~2000 candidates, auto-expands the report
strategyLab.constraints.presetExplain: One-click toggle for the candidate search space. "Default" preserves the current recommendation behaviour; "Diversification" and "Max diversification" widen the floating cap and step, auto-expand the exhaustive report, and adjust scoring weights so cross-term splits can win recommendation cards. Manually editing any parameter below auto-exits the preset and returns to a custom state.
strategyLab.constraints.presetExample: Example: want to see a 60% fixed-2y + 20% fixed-1y + 20% floating cross-term split? Switch to "Diversification".
strategyLab.constraints.maxSplitsExplain: Caps the number of sub-loan tranches your loan can be split into. Setting to 1 disables splitting entirely and only compares single-term lock strategies.
strategyLab.constraints.maxSplitsExample: Example: set to 3 and the system will search the optimal strategy across all valid 1-, 2-, and 3-tranche splits.
strategyLab.constraints.gridStepExplain: Allocation grid step across terms. Coarser step = fewer combinations = faster simulation. The default 10% balances richness and performance.
strategyLab.constraints.gridStepExample: Example: with a 10% step, a single-tranche split has 10 options: 10%, 20%, 30%, ..., 100%.
strategyLab.constraints.maxFloatingExpla: Caps the floating-rate (Floating / Offset / Revolving Credit) share of the loan. The system also guarantees a minimum fixed share of {fixedPct}% (i.e. 1 − floating share); the strategy generator derives that constraint internally.
strategyLab.constraints.maxFloatingExamp: Example: at 10%, the loan can have at most 10% floating; the other 90% must be locked to a fixed term.
strategyLab.constraints.budgetCapExplain: The maximum per-period payment you can afford. Used to count "budget overage" instances under high-rate scenarios and feeds the composite score.
strategyLab.constraints.budgetCapExample: Example: set to 5000 with fortnightly frequency; if a high-rate fortnightly payment hits 5200 the system records one overage.
strategyLab.preferencesIntro: The {n} weights below always sum to 100%. Raising one rescales the others proportionally. Affects only the "Preference-matched" card; rate-simulation parameters and other cards are unchanged.
strategyLab.warnings.highSimTitle: ⚠️ Projected simulation count is high: {count} (currently {strategies} strategies × {scenarios} scenarios)
strategyLab.warnings.highSimBody: Large simulation matrices significantly increase worker compute time (~{seconds}s+), and a dense Pareto set makes recommendations hard to distinguish. Consider simplifying one of the following:
strategyLab.warnings.tipMaxSplits: Lower "Maximum splits": currently {current} → recommend ≤ 3 (saves ~{pct}% of candidates)
strategyLab.warnings.tipStep: Increase "Combination grid step": currently {current}% → recommend 15% (saves ~{pct}% of candidates)
strategyLab.warnings.tipHorizon: Shorten "Simulation horizon": currently {current} yr → recommend ≤ 5 yr
strategyLab.warnings.tipFloating: Tighten "Maximum floating / Offset share": currently {current}% → recommend ≤ 30% (saves ~{pct}% of floating branches)
strategyLab.warnings.constraintsTight: Constraints are already tight; if you need to keep them, click "Start simulation" and accept the ~{seconds}s+ compute time.
strategyLab.warnings.inProgressBody: Above the {threshold} warning threshold. Either wait for the current run to finish, or cancel and tighten splits, increase step, or shorten horizon.

lab.welcome.title: Plan your mortgage in 60 seconds
lab.welcome.body: RatePath compares different fixed + floating combinations under future-rate scenarios and finds the best fit for you. Answer 6 quick questions to get started.
lab.progress.label: Question {current} / {total}
lab.q1.title: How much do you still owe?
lab.q1.hint: Enter the outstanding principal on your mortgage. Already-repaid amounts don't count.
lab.q2.title: How would you like to repay?
lab.q2.option.term: I want to pay it off in X years
lab.q2.term.before: I want to pay it off in
lab.q2.term.hint: Type the years directly into the X slot in the sentence.
lab.q2.payment.hint: Type the amount directly into the sentence.
lab.q2.term.label: Target years
lab.q2.term.aria: Number of years you want to pay off the loan in
lab.q2.payment.label: Per-period payment
lab.q2.payment.aria: The amount you can afford to pay each period
lab.q2.frequency.label: Repayment frequency
lab.q3.title: How do you think rates will move over the next year?
lab.q3.hint: This is just your expectation, not a conclusion; it only changes the forecast curve and the recommendation results.
lab.q4.title.rise: Do you think rates will keep rising over the next 3 years?
lab.q4.title.fall: Do you think rates will keep falling over the next 3 years?
lab.q4.hint: This is just your view on the medium-term path, not a certainty; it only changes the forecast curve and final recommendation results.
lab.q5.title: How uncertain do you think the rate outlook is?
lab.q5.hint: This is just your assessment of uncertainty; it changes the forecast width and the recommendation results.
lab.q6.title: How long do you want this forecast to run?
lab.q6.hint: Enter 3 to 10 years. This duration decides how far the OCR curve is drawn and how long the simulation runs.
lab.ocr.title: Here is our rate outlook
lab.ocr.hint: Based on your answers, we model three possible rate paths. Edit earlier answers and the curve updates live.
lab.ocr.summary.rise: Over the next year OCR is projected to rise ~{pct}%; {traj}.
lab.ocr.summary.fall: Over the next year OCR is projected to fall ~{pct}%; {traj}.

lab.premium.title: Advanced Lab
lab.premium.body: This is a premium feature in development. Soon you'll be able to customise preference weights, tune risk parameters, and try many more split combinations.
lab.detail.intro.riskAverse: Your answers suggest you're worried about rates rising, so we lock most of your principal into long-term fixed terms to keep your worst-case payment in check.
lab.detail.intro.neutral: This split balances total interest against stability by spreading your principal across different fixed terms, avoiding simultaneous refix.
lab.detail.intro.riskSeeking: Your answers suggest you're optimistic about rates falling, so we keep a meaningful floating slice to capture the lower total interest.
